source: RED-Green Belt Siem Reap network, facilitated with support from GIZ (German development cooperation) and Cambodian government partners, trifold brochure "វិធីដាំខ្នុរ" (How to Plant Jackfruit); practical training content credited to Ms. Chan Vin (អ្នកស្រី ចាន់វិន), a fruit-tree seedling vendor near Boeung Tonle Vil, Siem Reap; no publication date visible on the document.
text:
Dig the planting pit as a square-mouthed pit with an initial depth as shown in the brochure's diagram: roughly 8 units ("តឹក", a traditional local measure shown in the pit diagram — the exact metric equivalent is not confirmed) wide by 8 units deep, in an inverted-trapezoid cross-section. The diagram's note explains that the pit is measured so that the excavated topsoil can be conveniently used to backfill during pit preparation.

Before backfilling, sprinkle approximately 2 tablespoons of Furadan (a granular insecticide, sold as "ថ្នាំកណ្ដៀវ"/anti-termite or soil-pest treatment) into the bottom of the pit.

Then layer organic material into the pit: rice straw/husk, coconut coir or similar mulch material, dried leaves, and a layer of cow, chicken, and pig manure, placed as a distinct layer, with a top layer of soil covering it.

Once prepared, the pit should be left to rest for 2 to 3 weeks before planting.

Spacing between pits should be about 4 meters from one pit to the next.
